label: <DEL> step of long sequences (L>=8) whose first two tokens avoid a suppressor set
explanation: Fires only at the delimiter step (100% of activations at phase 1, i.e. when output of original token 0 starts), never in the original or copy phases. Rate rises steeply with length: L=9 (62% of mass), L=8 (32%), L=7 (5%), almost never at L<=6. Within long sequences, whether it fires depends on the earliest original tokens: first token in {v,2,i,h,o,c,k,n,r,d,l} gives about 0.5-0.8 firing rate at L>=8, while first token in {b,e,g,q,s,t,z,0} gives essentially zero (y,f,p,w low). The second token shows the same preference pattern but weaker, which suggests a graded sum over early-token identity rather than a single token detector. Predicate: delimiter step, L>=8, and neither of the first two tokens is in the suppressor set {b,e,g,q,s,t,z,0,y,f}; dev P=0.68 R=0.78 F1=0.73 mass recall 0.88. Misses are mostly L=7 sequences and weak activations; false positives are long sequences with neutral early tokens. Top activations (about 0.15-0.17) come from L=9 sequences starting with i/o/2/v, often with k/o as the second token. Adding a third-token condition did not help.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: 2, v, i, h, o, n; least: 0, e, b, g) and the second original token (most: o, k, 2, r, v, c; least: e, q, b, g); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=9, to_go=8, L=8 & t=8.
